title: Oscillators, PLLs and synthesizers
blurb: Explain how oscillators, phase-locked loops and DDS synthesizers generate frequencies, and how to keep an oscillator stable.

E7H01.why: The three common oscillator circuits are **Colpitts, Hartley and Pierce**.
E7H01.trap: Taft, Fenner and Beane are made up. Negative feedback doesn't oscillate.

E7H02.why: A **microphonic** is oscillator frequency change caused by **mechanical vibration**.
E7H02.trap: It isn't an audio chip or RF pickup on the microphone cable.

E7H03.why: A PLL is a servo loop of a **phase detector, low-pass filter, VCO and stable reference oscillator**.
E7H03.trap: A ratio detector and reactance modulator make an FM circuit, not a PLL.

E7H04.why: A Colpitts oscillator gets its positive feedback from a **capacitive divider**.
E7H04.trap: A tapped coil is the Hartley's feedback.

E7H05.why: A Pierce oscillator's positive feedback passes **through a quartz crystal**.
E7H05.trap: Tapped coil is Hartley. Link coupling and neutralizing capacitors aren't how a Pierce works.

E7H06.why: A PLL can do **frequency synthesis** (divider in the loop) and **FM demodulation** (the steering voltage is the audio).
E7H06.trap: It doesn't amplify power or do photovoltaic conversion.

E7H07.why: Vibration is the cause, so **mechanically isolate** the oscillator circuitry from its enclosure.
E7H07.trap: NP0 capacitors cure thermal drift, not vibration.

E7H08.why: **NP0** capacitors barely change value with temperature, so they reduce thermal drift.
E7H08.trap: Toroids and wirewound or non-inductive resistors don't fix drift.

E7H09.why: Phase accumulator, lookup table, DAC and low-pass anti-alias filter make a **direct digital synthesizer**.
E7H09.trap: A PLL synthesizer has a VCO and phase detector instead.

E7H10.why: The DDS lookup table holds **amplitude values that represent the desired waveform**, such as one sine cycle.
E7H10.trap: It stores no frequencies or phase relationships.

E7H11.why: A DDS's main impurities are **spurious signals at discrete frequencies**.
E7H11.trap: Broadband noise is not its main problem.

E7H12.why: A crystal runs on its marked frequency only when given its **specified parallel capacitance**.
E7H12.trap: Inductance, bias voltage and bias current don't set that frequency.

E7H13.why: GPS references, rubidium oscillators and temperature-controlled dielectric resonators are all used for accurate microwave oscillators.
